ActivityAttachment.description:
Attachment metadata as the UI consumes it (`@odo/core` FileUploadResponse
shape: numeric file_upload id, original/relative path, derived category).

attachment_file_upload_ids.description:
Each id refers to a row already in `asset.file_upload` (the UI
uploads through odo-asset first). Mirrors the contract on
`patron.photo.create`.

comments.description:
At least one of comments / attachments / external_links must be
provided; a no-op note isn't useful and would just add audit noise.

AttachmentResponse.description:
Shape the UI renders for an attachment (form-side AND incident-detail).
Pulled from `asset.file_upload` via `state.asset_client.get_files` on
read; never written by `current` directly (the UI uploads through
odo-asset before calling create / update).

category.description:
Echoed back to keep the UI's existing
`attachments.filter(a => a.category === 'photo')` rendering paths
unchanged. Derived from `mime_type`.

id.description:
The file's stable odo-asset uuid (matches the ids the client sends
in `attachment_file_upload_ids` / `remove_attachment_ids`).

mime_type.description:
MIME type echoed back so the UI can pick the right renderer.
The category is derived from this prefix (image/* → photo, etc.).

original_name.description: Original filename the user picked, suitable for display.

org_unit.description:
Org unit of the parent ban (handy for clients that want to scope
further actions against the letter without a second round-trip).

has_ban_letter.description:
True if at least one row exists in `generated_ban_letter` for
this ban — UI uses this to toggle "view letter" affordances.

patron_id.description: Alias of `patron` (the UI's `getPatronBans` consumers read this).

ban_letter_template.description:
If both `ban_letter_template` and `ban_letter_content` are set,
a `generated_ban_letter` row is created in the same transaction
and surfaced via the response's `ban_letter_id`.

case_number.description:
Stored in the `ban.created` activity_log event_data, not on the
patron_ban row. Read back via the activity feed.

starts_at.description:
All ISO-8601 timestamps with offset. Omitted dates default per
the constants above (lifts_at = now + 30d; archives_at = lifts_at
+ 30d for bans, never auto-archives for trespasses).

ban_letter_id.description:
id of the `generated_ban_letter` row that was created alongside
the ban, if the caller passed `ban_letter_content`. None otherwise.

attachment_file_upload_ids.description:
File-upload row ids the UI has already created via
`POST /api/v1/odo/asset/upload`. Each id becomes one
`incidents.attachments` join row pointing back at the file.
Empty / omitted = no attachments. The legacy contract embedded
full file metadata under `metadata.attachments`; that path
double-wrote the file row and is gone.

metadata.description:
Free-form metadata. One nested key is extracted out and handled
specially:
  - `external_links`: Vec<CreateExternalLink> — written to
    incidents.external_link (and removed from the metadata that's
    persisted on the incident row itself).

`pending_bans` / `pending_extends` are also read from metadata
and handled by `bans::apply_pending_bans` — they're not stripped
(so the original intent survives in the persisted blob for
audit) but they do not affect the row otherwise.

The UI sometimes double-stringifies this (sends `metadata: "{...}"`
instead of `metadata: {...}`). We try the object form first and fall
back to parsing a JSON string.

created_ban_ids.description:
ids of bans created via `metadata.pending_bans[]`. Empty when
the form didn't toggle any inline bans. Best-effort: bad
entries are skipped with a warn-log, not surfaced as errors.

extended_ban_ids.description:
ids of bans extended via `metadata.pending_extends[]`. Same
best-effort semantics as `created_ban_ids`.

file_upload_id.description:
id of the row in `asset.file_upload` that the UI already
uploaded via odo-asset's `/upload` endpoint. We trust the id
exists; bad ids fail the FK constraint with a 4xx.

first_name.description:
Patrons created on the fly may carry minimal info (e.g. just a
first name during incident capture), so most fields are optional.

auto_resolved_review_id.description:
ID of the synthetic `resolved` review row written by the
auto-resolution path, if any.

id.description:
ID of the primary review row that was just inserted. Auto-
resolution may also have inserted a second `resolved` row; its ID
is in `auto_resolved_review_id` when present.

result.description: Wire-format string of the recorded review result.

was_auto_resolved.description:
True when this action implicitly resolved the incident because
the actor was the final reviewer and the action was a progressing
one (submit/approve/approve-with-edits).

file_removed.description:
True when the on-disk file was actually unlinked. The DB row
for the upload is marked deleted either way.

file_upload_id.description:
id of the underlying `asset.file_upload` row that was
soft-deleted via odo-asset. Returned so the UI can correlate.

bans_lifted.description: Count of active bans that were lifted as part of the deletion.

archived_by.description:
Allows manually marking a ban archived via this endpoint.
`archive_ban` is the preferred path; this exists for the rare
edit-and-archive-in-one-call flow.

ban_letter_template.description:
Same letter-attach flow as create. Triggers
`ban.letter_regenerated` rather than `ban.letter_generated`.

case_number.description:
Stored in the `ban.updated` event_data when changed. We compare
against the most recent value of the same key in the ban's
activity feed (case_number / law_enforcement_agency don't live
on the patron_ban row).

generated_by_org.description:
Org that issued the letter; usually equals the ban's org_unit
but the legacy lets the caller distinguish so we do too.

incident.description:
Optionally associates the extension with an incident — usually
the incident that prompted the extension. Persisted in the
activity log row and on any generated letter.

lifts_at.description: New end date. Required — extend without a target is meaningless.

oneOf.description: Null when no letter with the given id exists.

org_unit.description:
Optional org_unit to scope statistics to that org unit and its
descendants. When None, stats span the entire tree.

oneOf.description:
Cursor from a prior call's response (`next_cursor`). Resumes
the keyset-paged scan right after the last incident examined
(not the last incident *returned*). Omit to start from the
oldest open incident.

limit.description:
Cap on the number of visible rows returned in this page.
Defaults to `DEFAULT_PAGE_LIMIT` and is clamped to `MAX_PAGE_LIMIT`.
The inner DB scan may examine more rows than this — the cap
only controls the visible-row count in the response.

org_unit.description:
Org unit to scope the search (descendants included). Defaults to
the root org unit when omitted (resolved via odo-org).

day.description: Day of week, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday, in the report timezone.

hour.description: Hour of day, 0-23, in the report timezone.

attachments.description:
Attachments bound to this incident, decorated with file
metadata fetched from odo-asset. Returned when
`options.with_attachments = true`. None means the caller didn't
ask, not that there are no attachments.

external_name.description:
Populated for `party_type = "external"` rows (the schema's check
constraint requires it). The legacy read path silently dropped this
— the UI's external-party display logic was relying on a field
the server never sent.

include_archived.description:
When false (default), filter out archived bans. Trespasses are
considered archived once `archived_by` is set; non-trespass bans
are considered archived once their `archives_at` is reached.

org_unit.description:
Scope bans to this org unit and its descendants. Trespasses are
always visible regardless of org_unit (cross-location semantics).

resolution.description:
"primary" keeps the primary's ban and lifts the secondary's;
"secondary" the reverse. Anything else is ignored.

custom_value.description:
Only used when `resolution = "custom"`. Free-form JSON to
match the legacy contract.

field.description:
Which patron field this resolution applies to. Empty for
non-field conflict kinds (e.g. photo).

resolution.description:
"primary" (keep the primary patron's value), "secondary" (copy
from secondary), or "custom" (use `custom_value`).

type.description:
Conflict kind, e.g. "field_conflict" / "primary_photo". The
handler dispatches on `field` for field_conflict resolutions;
`type` is kept for forward-compatibility with future
conflict kinds and matches the UI's wire shape.

lift_ban_ids.description: IDs of trespass ban rows to lift as part of the merge.

resolution.description:
"primary" or "secondary"; informational only — the actual
trespasses to lift are listed in `lift_ban_ids`.

cells.description: Sparse: only cells with a non-zero count.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone the day/hour cells were computed in — the selected
org unit's timezone (or the root's when unscoped).

PatronDetailRow.description:
Wire shape mirrors the patrons table row plus a derived `age_range_label`.
We don't pin every field to a typed struct because the UI's
`transformToPatronDetails` reads a wide set of columns and treats the
`patron` field as opaque; passing the row through preserves forward-
compatibility with schema additions.

has_active_bans.description:
Only return patrons with at least one active non-trespass ban
(in scope, when `org_unit` is set; anywhere otherwise).

has_visible_trespass.description:
Only return patrons with at least one visible trespass.
Trespasses are cross-location, so this gate ignores `org_unit`.

is_unknown.description: Exact-match on the patron's is_unknown flag. Omit for both.

org_unit.description:
Org unit to scope incident / ban joins to. Expanded to
descendants via `OrgServiceClient`. Omit to search across all
orgs.

query.description:
Free-text search across first/last/alias/library_card/email.
Whitespace-split into terms; per-term hits are OR'd across
the fields, and terms are AND'd together.

sort_dir.description:
"asc" (default) or "desc". Drives the MIN/MAX choice on the
sort aggregate and the ORDER BY direction.

sort_incident_date.description:
Sort by aggregated incident date (MIN/MAX(occurred_at)).
Mutually exclusive with `sort_lift_date`; lift_date wins.

sort_lift_date.description:
Sort by ban / trespass lift date. Ascending picks the soonest
to expire; descending picks the furthest out.

active_ban_count.description: Same shape for active non-trespass bans.

ban_location_names.description: Comma-separated distinct org labels for active-ban orgs.

ban_max_lifts_at.description: Sort-aware MIN/MAX of visible non-trespass ban `lifts_at`.

incident_count.description:
SUM of per-(patron, org) incident counts (scoped to descendants
when `org_unit` is set; over all orgs otherwise).

incident_org_unit_id.description:
Org of the "representative" incident for display. Picked as the
(patron, org_unit) row with the latest incident date — same
approximation the legacy made.

last_incident_date.description:
MAX(occurred_at) over scoped incidents in default sort mode.
Swapped for the sort-aware aggregate when `sort_incident_date`.

primary_photo_path.description:
Primary photo's `relative_path` — null when the patron has no
primary photo. Sourced from the view's join through
`asset.file_upload`.

sort_incident_date.description:
Sort-aware MIN/MAX of scoped incident dates when
`sort_incident_date = true`.

total_incidents_count.description: Distinct incidents this patron is involved in.

PendingReviewsCursor.description:
Keyset cursor for `get_pending_reviews`. Pair `(created_at, id)`
uniquely orders the open-incident set under
`ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC` — perfect for stable pagination
without offsets.

oneOf.description:
Pass back unchanged on the next request to resume. `None` when
the inner DB scan reached the end of the open-incident set.

ReportBucket.description:
Time-bucket size for the over-time reports. The UI picks day for short
ranges and month for long ones. Buckets are UTC calendar units.

bucket.description: Bucket start date (YYYY-MM-DD), bucketed by resolved_at.

median_days.description:
Median days from occurred_at to resolved_at across them; None for
buckets where nothing was resolved.

result.description: Wire string matching the DB enum value (e.g. "submitted", "approved-with-edits").

StatusFilter.description:
Incident-status filter for the count-by reports. The over-time series
are exempt (their series already encode status), and the review-status
report is pinned to open incidents (every closed incident's latest
result is "resolved", so the breakdown degenerates).

SummaryRequest.description:
Filters for the KPI summary. Deliberately has no status field: the
tiles themselves break the counts down by status.

median_days_to_resolve.description:
Median days from occurred_at to resolved_at across the incidents
resolved in the period; None when nothing was resolved.

resolved_incidents.description:
Incidents resolved during the period (by resolved_at, matching the
over-time chart's resolved series).

total_incidents.description: Incidents that occurred in the period.

add_attachment_file_upload_ids.description:
file_upload row ids to bind to this incident, same contract as
create's `attachment_file_upload_ids`: odo-asset already wrote the
`asset.file_upload` row at upload time; we only add the
`incidents.attachments` join row.

is_deleted.description:
One-way latch: setting `true` soft-deletes the incident. `false`
does nothing. Legacy did not support undelete via this endpoint
either.

is_resolved.description:
One-way latch: setting `true` resolves an unresolved incident
(sets `resolved_at` + `resolved_by`). `false` does nothing — to
reopen, use `incident.review.create` with `result: "reopened"`,
which goes through the review-chain permission checks.

metadata.description:
Same `JSON.stringify(...)` quirk as create: the UI sends this
pre-stringified, so we use the shared deserializer that unwraps
the outer string layer. Without this, the wrapping piles up on
each save (`{}` → `"{}"` → `"\"{}\""`) and breaks downstream
readers.

remove_attachment_ids.description:
file_upload ids to unlink from this incident. These match the
`id` field returned for each attachment by `incident/get` (which
is the file_upload id, not the join-row id). We delete the
`incidents.attachments` join rows pointing at these files; the
`asset.file_upload` rows are left intact — deleting the file is
odo-asset's `files/delete` endpoint's job.

template_ids.description:
Full-replace semantics: passing `Some([..])` clears the
incident's existing `incident_template_map` rows and inserts a
new mapping for each id. Passing `Some([])` clears all
templates. `None` (the field omitted from the payload) leaves
the existing mapping untouched — "no change" rather than
"clear", same shape as the legacy port (CRT-88).
